ground.purpose: Cool-gray page ground under white cards: separates cards in daylight without heavy borders; an all-white page reads as plain.

flame.purpose: Daily streak only (top-bar pill, Day streak tile). Combo uses the bolt in --combo.

combo.purpose: Combo bolt and counter only (.sbar .meta.combo, .f-combo .ic); sits outside the lecture, streak, XP and answer colors.

l8.purpose: Lecture 8; also the selected-ungraded choice and the Practice-test bubble.

on-fill.purpose: Literal #fff on green, red and lecture fills; not a CSS variable in the build.

headline-hero.purpose: Lecture name in the home hero; max 15ch, balanced.

body.purpose: Base text; Nunito ships 500-900, so 500 is the floor.

stat.purpose: Streak and XP pills; tabular figures.

label.purpose: Row subtitles, mastery counts, question meta.

label-sm.purpose: Status tags (Up next, N to fix, Done).

shadows.name: soft-lift
shadows.purpose: The one ambient shadow: cards, rows, pills, hero, score, flashcards. CSS var --shadow.

shadows.name: soft-lift-dark
shadows.purpose: Soft Lift under the dark theme.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Typed-answer field on focus, with an L5 border.

shadows.name: pressable-edge
shadows.purpose: Not a box-shadow: the depth of pressable controls. 5px rest (4px segments/symbol keys, 6px flashcard faces), 2px plus translateY(3px) on press.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--go) 70%, var(--ink)); outline-offset: 3px

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default ease-out (CSS var --ease): pop, rise, progress fill, toast.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Counters on change, correct answer card.

motion.name: shake
motion.purpose: Wrong choice or wrong typed answer.

motion.name: confetti-fall
motion.purpose: 18 hand-placed pieces (CONFETTI list: x%, y%, rotation) in two top-corner clusters of the score card (x 4-17% and 80-93%, y 6-36%), colored l5, l6, l7, l8, go, xp in turn; staggered (k % 6) * 80ms.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> all animation and transition none; confetti still rendered at its placed positions (top: var(--y), rotate(var(--r)), opacity .85)
motion.purpose: Everything static; confetti stays as the two still corner clusters instead of disappearing.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.purpose: Max width of the single centered column (.wrap).

breakpoints.name: hover
breakpoints.purpose: Gates choice hover fill and keyboard-shortcut hints.

lectureScope.mechanism: Classes .t-L5..t-L8 set --c to --l5..--l8; components mix from var(--c).

iconography.source: app.js object P plus inline SVG in index.html
iconography.duotone: back layer fill currentColor at opacity .25
iconography.set: arrow, chevron, check, cross, close, target, cards, watch, turn, flame (streak), bolt (combo, in --combo), gem (XP)

stickyBars.session: sticky, 90% ground + blur(10px), 64px; replaces top bar in rounds
stickyBars.flashcard-sort: sticky bottom, solid ground, padding 12px 16px calc(14px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); card min-height = max(face scrollHeight, 300px, viewport room)

narrative.overview:
SignalsGym is a training floor that fits in one hand. Every screen is a stack of rounded, softly shadowed white cards on a cool-gray ground, and every action is a chunky, pressable button that physically sinks when tapped. The mood is friendly, upbeat and encouraging: heavy rounded type, saturated but clean color, and small bursts of celebration when the student gets something right. It is the study-app category standard (Gizmo, Duolingo, Quizlet) played straight and finished properly, applied to one student's own DSP reviewer.

Color carries meaning, not decoration. Green means go and correct, red means wrong and to-fix, gold is XP, the orange flame is the daily streak, a teal bolt is the answer combo, and each of the four lectures owns a hue (L5 sky blue, L6 pink, L7 orange, L8 violet) that tints whatever surface is about that lecture. Density is comfortable and thumb-sized: 44px minimum targets, 58px primary buttons, 64px answer cards, and one 600px column even on desktop.

The world was chosen by the user after a harsh, boxy airport-signage direction was rejected as not fun. It refuses that world (monochrome, sign-like, square, sterile), and it equally refuses the cheap version of its own category: purple gradients, emoji icons and washed-out, low-contrast chips.
keyCharacteristics: White cards on a cool-gray ground (never an all-white page), lifted by one soft two-layer shadow.
Pressable buttons with a darker 5px bottom edge that compresses to 2px on press.
Four lecture hues applied through one variable, tinting badges, heroes, include toggles, bars and flashcard backs.
Self-hosted Nunito, heavy (800 to 900) for everything read at a glance.
Authored duotone SVG pictograms in currentColor; no emoji, no icon font.
Celebration on success (pop, confetti), a shake on a miss; under reduced motion everything holds still and the confetti stays as two static corner clusters.

rules.name: The Lecture Owns Its Color Rule
rules.body: A surface about one lecture takes that lecture's hue through `--c` and mixes from it; never hard-code a lecture hex into a component. The same four hues also serve as the general accent family: L5 Sky marks focus and selection in setup (pressed segment, focused answer field) and the Flashcards bubble; L8 Violet marks a chosen-but-ungraded choice and the Practice-test bubble.

rules.name: The Green Means Go Rule
rules.body: Green is reserved for moving forward and for being right. A screen's forward action is the green pressable button; red appears only for wrong answers, mistakes to fix, and the explicit "still learning" sort.

rules.name: The Gold Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Gold and flame orange mark rewards only: XP, mastery done and the daily streak. They never decorate neutral UI.

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: The orange flame means the daily streak and nothing else. The answer combo is the authored bolt in Combo Teal, in the session-bar counter and on the Best combo tile; Combo Teal is used for nothing else.

rules.name: The Heavy Heading Rule
rules.body: Anything read at a glance (headings, buttons, counts, badges, tags) sets at 800 or 900. Body and explanations stay at 500 to 600; nothing renders below 500.

rules.name: The Tabular Counter Rule
rules.body: Every changing number (XP, streak, combo, score, stats, summary values) uses tabular figures so it can pop without the row reflowing.

rules.name: The Pressable Edge Rule
rules.body: Anything the student presses to act (primary and secondary buttons, answer choices, segments, symbol keys) carries a darker bottom edge (5px; 4px on segments and symbol keys; 6px on flashcard faces) and on press drops 3px while the edge compresses to 2px. Cards that only navigate (mode rows, lecture cards) lift 1px on hover instead, and mode rows sink 1px on press. Information cards and the include toggle never get an edge.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is one ambient shadow token. Controls with borders do not also take a shadow.

dos: **Do** give every pressable action the bottom edge and the 3px press (The Pressable Edge Rule).
**Do** scope lecture color through `--c` with `.t-L5` to `.t-L8` and mix tints from it (13% hero, 10 to 12% selection, 15% bubbles).
**Do** set headings, labels and numbers at 800 to 900 in Nunito, and keep the font self-hosted; the app must work offline.
**Do** draw icons as authored 24px SVG in currentColor with 2.2 to 3.2px round strokes and a 25%-opacity fill for the duotone layer.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more and primary buttons at 58px.
**Do** celebrate correct answers and finished rounds, and make every animation static under `prefers-reduced-motion` (keep the confetti as its still corner clusters rather than removing it).
**Do** show the combo with the bolt in Combo Teal and keep the flame for the daily streak (The One Flame Rule).
**Do** keep the page ground cool gray and reserve white for cards.
**Do** keep light as the default theme and define every new neutral, tint and lecture color for dark as well.
donts: **Don't** use emoji as icons, or an icon font.
**Don't** use purple or multi-color gradients as backgrounds or fills; tints are flat color-mixes.
**Don't** ship low-contrast chips or toggles: unpressed segments keep Ink Muted labels and include toggles keep a visible 2px Soft Line border.
**Don't** fade a whole disabled choice; mute its text to Ink Muted and dim only its key.
**Don't** go harsh, monochrome, square or sign-like (the rejected signage world): no square corners, no all-caps signage type, no black-and-yellow bands.
**Don't** spend green, gold or flame on decoration; they carry go/correct, XP and streak only.
**Don't** add a second shadow, or put a shadow on a bordered control.
